decisions.reason: As a visible extension of the firm’s core tariff and calculation offer in a growing market, it is likely to meet internal aspirations well enough that management keeps it while exploiting existing data and platform resources.

This product is close to the established business and was given its own page, so with moderate organisational slack the firm is likely to retain it unless early demand clearly falls below expectations.

A regional electricity tariff calculator fits the firm’s core customer problems and digital platform direction, making it more likely to stay on the market than be withdrawn after only a short trial period.

Although strategically related to the core offer, its weaker website prominence suggests more uncertainty, but in a growing industry the firm would still more likely keep it for further learning than redeploy resources immediately.

The area definition tool appears to support the firm’s broader integrated platform and data capabilities, so it likely clears aspiration thresholds or benefits enough from complementarities to be retained.

This comparison product is close to the established offer but only lightly promoted, implying a more tentative commitment, yet the firm still likely keeps it because software-side carrying costs are limited and results remain uncertain after launch.
